description: Days used only in combined programmes. An integration day is added when both technologies are requested; a capstone is used when every requested technology is in its applies_to list.

day.topic: Python on AWS: Automation with boto3 and Lambda
subtopics: Credentials from roles instead of keys
Writing a Lambda handler in Python
day.lab_task: Write a Python Lambda function with boto3 that resizes images uploaded to S3 and records metadata in DynamoDB, with unit tests that mock AWS using moto.
day.deliverable: Function code, Lambda layer, IAM policy and passing tests
checks: Upload a test image to the input bucket
Resized image and a metadata item are created
Run the unit tests with the network off
Remove the role's DynamoDB permission and upload again
Function logs a ClientError with AccessDenied and does not crash
objectives: Automate AWS from Python with boto3
Build and test Python Lambda functions
Handle AWS errors and permissions in code

day.topic: Python on Azure: Azure SDK and Azure Functions
subtopics: Azure SDK for Python client libraries
Writing an Azure Function in Python
Bindings in the Python v2 programming model
Least-privilege role assignments for Python code
day.lab_task: Write a Python Azure Function that resizes images uploaded to Blob Storage and writes metadata to Table Storage, authenticating with managed identity, with unit tests that mock the SDK.
day.deliverable: Function code, role assignments and passing tests
checks: Upload a test image to the input container
Resized image and a metadata row are created
Search the code and settings for storage keys
Remove the identity's role and upload again
Function logs an authorisation error and does not crash
objectives: Automate Azure from Python with the Azure SDK
Build and test Python Azure Functions
Authenticate Python code with managed identity

day.topic: AWS and Azure Compared: Service Mapping and Multi-Cloud Decisions
subtopics: Mapping core services between AWS and Azure
Identity: IAM compared with Entra ID and Azure RBAC
When multi-cloud helps and when it adds risk
day.lab_task: Deploy the same small container web service on AWS (ECS Fargate) and Azure (Container Apps) with Terraform, then compare setup effort, monthly cost and operational differences.
day.deliverable: Terraform code for both clouds, a service mapping table and a one-page comparison with a recommendation
checks: Same service responds on AWS and Azure
Monthly cost for both uses the official calculators with the same assumptions
Choice is justified with at least three criteria
objectives: Map AWS and Azure services to each other
Compare clouds on cost and operations with evidence
Decide when multi-cloud is justified

day.topic: Integrated Capstone: Multi-Cloud Python Service on AWS and Azure
subtopics: Requirements and architecture for both clouds
Python API with tests and a container image
Deployment to AWS and Azure with Terraform
Secrets with Secrets Manager and Key Vault
Monitoring and alerts on both clouds
Verify acceptance criteria, cost comparison and demo
day.lab_task: Build a tested Python API, containerise it, deploy it to AWS and Azure with Terraform using each cloud's secret store and monitoring, then demonstrate failover between them and present a cost comparison.
day.deliverable: Repository with application, tests and Terraform for both clouds, monitoring screenshots, cost comparison and a 15-minute demo
checks: Run the test suite and both deployments from the pipeline
Tests pass and the API responds on both clouds
Stop the AWS deployment during the demo
Traffic is served from Azure as designed
None found; both clouds read secrets from their secret stores
objectives: Deliver one Python service on two clouds end to end
Apply security and monitoring on AWS and Azure
Compare and justify multi-cloud design choices

day.topic: Integrated Capstone: Python Service on AWS
subtopics: Deployment to Lambda or ECS with infrastructure as code
day.lab_task: Build a tested Python API and deploy it to AWS with infrastructure as code, secrets in Secrets Manager, least-privilege roles and CloudWatch alarms, then present it.
day.deliverable: Repository with application, tests and infrastructure code, dashboard and a 15-minute demo
checks: Tests pass and the API responds
objectives: Deliver a Python service on AWS end to end
Apply security and monitoring
Explain design decisions

day.topic: Integrated Capstone: Python Service on Azure
subtopics: Deployment to Container Apps or Functions with infrastructure as code
day.lab_task: Build a tested Python API and deploy it to Azure with infrastructure as code, secrets in Key Vault, managed identity and Application Insights alerts, then present it.
day.deliverable: Repository with application, tests and infrastructure code, workbook and a 15-minute demo
checks: Tests pass and the API responds
objectives: Deliver a Python service on Azure end to end
Apply security and monitoring
Explain design decisions

day.topic: Integrated Capstone: Multi-Cloud Web Application on AWS and Azure
subtopics: Requirements and architecture for both clouds
Networking and identity on each cloud
Secrets and monitoring on each cloud
Verify acceptance criteria, cost comparison and demo
day.lab_task: Deploy one containerised web application to AWS and Azure with Terraform, secure and monitor it on both, set up DNS failover, and present a cost and operations comparison.
day.deliverable: Terraform code for both clouds, monitoring screenshots, failover test and a 15-minute demo
checks: Open the application through the shared DNS name
DNS fails over to the other cloud
Both clouds are costed with the same assumptions
objectives: Deploy one application on two clouds
Apply security and monitoring on AWS and Azure
Compare clouds with evidence
